common_name: Lollipop Itoh Peony (Candy-Striped Yellow Intersectional Peony)

planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in fall 4-6 weeks before the ground freezes, with eyes no more than 1-2 in below the soil surface, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade in hot climates.

directions: Plant roots with the eyes no more than 1-2 in below the soil surface in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade, giving afternoon shade where summers are hottest. Lollipop produces large, semi- to fully double, creamy yellow flowers heavily streaked, flecked, and striped in candy red to raspberry pink, so that no two blooms open quite the same, opening from May into June on neat, mounding plants. Like other intersectional hybrids it combines tree-peony flower size and color range with the reliable die-back-to-the-ground habit and cold hardiness of herbaceous peonies, and its sturdy stems hold the heavy, fragrant blooms upright without staking. Deeply cut, dark green foliage stays attractive and disease-resistant well past bloom, and established clumps resent disturbance, so divide only when necessary.

common_name: Age of Gold Tree Peony (Saunders Scarlet-and-Gold Hybrid Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Plant in deep, humus-rich, well-drained soil in a permanent site, since tree peonies resent being moved once established. Age of Gold is an American Saunders hybrid tree peony, registered in 1948, bearing large semi-double flowers in a striking bicolor of bright gold overlaid with scarlet-red flares radiating from the center, opening in mid spring on a vigorous, upright shrub. Bred from Paeonia suffruticosa crossed with the yellow-flowered P. lutea/delavayi group, it helped pioneer the warm gold and bronze color range that later Saunders and Daphnis hybrids built on. Give full sun where summers are mild but afternoon shade and reliable moisture in hot, humid climates, and avoid heavy pruning since flower buds form on the prior year's wood.

common_name: High Noon Tree Peony (Gold Medal Lemon-Yellow Saunders Hybrid Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Plant in deep, humus-rich, well-drained soil in a permanent site, since tree peonies resent being moved once established. High Noon is an American Paeonia lutea hybrid tree peony bred by Professor A. P. Saunders and introduced in 1952, bearing lemon-yellow buds that open to buttery yellow, semi-double, lightly fragrant flowers 6-8 in across with deep red flares at the base of each petal. It grows upright and slightly spreading on a fast, sturdy framework, and unusually for a tree peony it can produce a light second flush of bloom in late summer or early fall. Winner of the American Peony Society Gold Medal and the RHS Award of Garden Merit, it remains one of the standard yellow tree peonies for gardeners. Give full sun where summers are mild but afternoon shade and reliable moisture in hot, humid climates, and avoid heavy pruning since flower buds form on the prior year's wood.

common_name: Leda Tree Peony (Mauve-Pink Japanese Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union 4-6 inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Plant in deep, humus-rich, well-drained soil in a permanent site, since tree peonies resent being moved once established. Leda bears large, semi-double, mauve-pink flowers 6-8 in across, each petal marked with reddish-purple flares at the base surrounding a prominent boss of golden-yellow stamens, opening in mid spring on a full, deeply cut canopy of foliage that is pale underneath. Its soft, cool coloring and strong flower substance have kept it in circulation among tree peony specialists as a reliable mauve-toned selection. Give full sun where summers are mild but afternoon shade and reliable moisture in hot, humid climates, and avoid heavy pruning since flower buds form on the prior year's wood.
